The RFUS technology developed here upon further verification and pilot-scale evaluation can be implemented in commercial manufacturing operations. This technology and the relevant equipment and drying system can be successfully integrated in commercial manufacturing of paper, consumer products, biomaterials, food, and other industries in the United States. Recommendations and Commercialization Application of RF energy at various locations on the paper machine is a viable approach in imparting auxiliary energy to increase the drying rate and energy intensity. This is especially effective at higher basis weights and at higher sheet moisture contents. For paper machines with currently limited drying capacity, RF applications can be considered. At lower moisture contents, RF is not as effective as a drying method, but more suitable to even out local variations in moisture content profiles across the width of the machine. US applications in the pockets between the cylinders integrated with the pocket ventilation systems can be used to improve the drying rate throughout the drying section. With optimal integration of RFUS technology with RF and US applied at various moisture contents (locations) on the paper machine, drying rate profile with warm up, constant rate and falling rate sections can be effectively altered and the overall drying performance can be significantly improved. We recommend that the RFUS technology developed here be further verified and pilot-scale evaluation be conducted before implemented in commercial manufacturing operations. With continued development and wide scale availability of renewable energy throughout the US, the commercial implementation of RFUS technology will also help improve the carbon intensity and GHG emission reductions of paper manufacturing. The RFUS technology developed here upon further verification and pilot-scale evaluation can be considered for commercial implementation. This technology and the relevant equipment and drying system can be potentially be integrated in commercial manufacturing of paper, consumer products, biomaterials, food, and other industries in the United States. There are practical limitations related to applying, especially contact US, in the pockets and they warrant further study. The primary customers for the RFUS equipment/technology would be the paper and board manufacturers in the United States and around the world. The target market can extend beyond 60 DE-EE0009395 commodity paper manufacturing to specialty papers and paperboard, and other bio-based materials. There are limited RF and US component technologies and suppliers in the United States. A number of equipment and other suppliers to the industry service the paper mills and would be likely partners for distribution/integration of RFUS equipment made by the RF and US system manufacturers. Market barriers for entry of new energy-saving technologies in the papermaking process are: limited R&D capability within mill owner/operators, reluctance to assume risk for first-of-a-kind processes, and poorly understand economic case for energy and carbon reduction. This project attempts to address some of these barriers through bringing R&D resources/ideas from other industries to bear on this problem, technology de-risking, providing a better understanding of the process economic and environmental drivers.
